'''Peercoin''', also known as '''Peer-to-Peer Coin''', '''PP Coin''', or '''PPC''', is a  [[cryptocurrency]] utilizing both [[proof-of-stake]] and [[proof-of-work system|proof-of-work]] systems.<ref name="arstechnica">{{cite web |url=https://arstechnica.com/business/2013/05/wary-of-bitcoin-a-guide-to-some-other-cryptocurrencies/2/ |title=Wary of Bitcoin? A guide to some other cryptocurrencies |website=Arstechnica |date=2013-05-11 |access-date=2017-06-14 |archive-date=2016-10-18 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161018121716/http://arstechnica.com/business/2013/05/wary-of-bitcoin-a-guide-to-some-other-cryptocurrencies/2/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="ZhaoYangLuo2021">{{cite conference| last1 = Zhao | first1 = Wenbing | last2 = Yang | first2 = Shunkun | last3 = Luo | first3 = Xiong | last4 = Zhou | first4 = Jiong | title = On PeerCoin Proof of Stake for Blockchain Consensus | date = 26 March 2021 | publisher = ACM | doi = 10.1145/3460537.3460547 | book-title = ICBCT'21: The 3rd International Conference on Blockchain Technology | pages=129–134 | url = }}</ref> It is notable as the first cryptocurrency to implement the proof-of-stake [[Consensus_(computer_science)|consensus mechanism]].<ref>{{Cite journal| doi = 10.1093/rfs/hhaa075| issn = 0893-9454| volume = 34| issue = 3| pages = 1156–1190| last = Saleh| first = Fahad| title = Blockchain without Waste: Proof-of-Stake| journal = [[The Review of Financial Studies]]| date = 2021-03-01}}</ref>

==History==

Peercoin is based on an August 2012<ref>{{Cite web |last=Daly |first=Lyle |title=Peercoin: Defined and Explained |url=https://www.fool.com/investing/stock-market/market-sectors/financials/cryptocurrency-stocks/peercoin/ |access-date=2023-12-25 |website=The Motley Fool |language=en |archive-date=2024-02-04 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240204113700/https://www.fool.com/investing/stock-market/market-sectors/financials/cryptocurrency-stocks/peercoin/ |url-status=live }}</ref> paper that listed the authors as Scott Nadal and Sunny King. King, who also created [[Primecoin]], is a pseudonym.<ref>{{cite news | date=24 November 2013 | title=In Bitcoin's orbit: Rival virtual currencies vie for acceptance | work=The New York Times | first=Nathaniel | last=Popper | url=https://dealbook.nytimes.com/2013/11/24/in-bitcoins-orbit-rival-virtual-currencies-vie-for-acceptance/ | access-date=25 February 2014 | archive-date=1 February 2014 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140201171500/http://dealbook.nytimes.com/2013/11/24/in-bitcoins-orbit-rival-virtual-currencies-vie-for-acceptance/ | url-status=live }}</ref>

The Peercoin source code is distributed under the [[MIT]]/[[X11]] software license.{{Citation needed|date=May 2024}}

==Economics==

Peercoin uses both the proof-of-work and proof-of-stake algorithms.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Frankenfield |first1=Jake |title=Peercoin Definition |url=https://www.investopedia.com/terms/p/peercoin.asp |website=Investopedia |access-date=30 April 2023 |archive-date=3 June 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210603040319/https://www.investopedia.com/terms/p/peercoin.asp |url-status=live }}</ref> Both are used to spread the distribution of new coins. During its primary years, Peercoin relied heavily on PoW, although there has now been a transition to PoS.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Daly |first1=Lyle |title=What is Peercoin? |url=https://www.fool.com/investing/stock-market/market-sectors/financials/cryptocurrency-stocks/peercoin/ |website=The Motley Fool |access-date=30 April 2023 |archive-date=30 April 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230430023335/https://www.fool.com/investing/stock-market/market-sectors/financials/cryptocurrency-stocks/peercoin/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Proof-of-stake is used to secure the network: The chain with longest PoS coin age wins in case of a blockchain split-up.

To target a global 1% annual inflation rate, individual stakes typically receive a 3 - 5% annual reward, as only a minority of coins are actively staked.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Daly |first1=Lyle |title=Minters Get Richer? |url=https://www.peercoin.net/blog/minters-get-richer/ |website=Peercoin |access-date=10 December 2024}}</ref> This reward is based on a dynamic portion (75% of the reward) and a static portion (25% of the reward).<ref>{{cite web |last1=Daly |first1=Lyle |title=Peercoin Inflation Adjustment |url=https://www.peercoin.net/blog/peercoin-inflation-adjustment/ |website=Peercoin |access-date=10 December 2024}}</ref> The dynamic portion of the reward for an individual stake is based on the number of coins, their unspent age, and degree of global staking participation. Stake-for-Stake, periods of low (high) global staking participation will result in a higher (lower) dynamic reward. The static portion of the reward is based on the fraction of the existing total coin supply minted on average in a year, and is awarded regardless of stake size. As of December 2024, the static reward for a proof-of-stake block is approximately 1.4 PPC.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://charts.peercoinexplorer.net/staticreward/2/linear/default |title=Static reward |website=Peercoin Charts |access-date=10 December 2024}}</ref>

A transaction fee prevents spam and is burned (instead of being collected by a miner), benefiting the overall network.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Nagalim |title=A Smarter Fee |url=https://www.peercoin.net/blog/a-smarter-fee/ |website=Peercoin |date=14 March 2021 |access-date=30 April 2023 |archive-date=30 April 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230430023336/https://www.peercoin.net/blog/a-smarter-fee/ |url-status=live }}</ref>
